Vocal

/VO-kul/ — rhymes with local · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Vocal describes someone who openly and freely expresses their opinions.

She was vocal about the broken microscopes, raising them at every meeting.

Worked Example

At a faculty meeting, one teacher remained vocal about the outdated equipment, naming specific problems and refusing to drop the issue.

Vocal is more precise than simply 'outspoken' here because it emphasizes that the teacher not only speaks opinions but freely, openly, and persistently raises them — vocal captures that active, unreserved quality of speaking up.

How Vocal Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

outspoken

outspoken: frank and direct in stating opinions

talkative

talkative: fond of talking a great deal

expressive

expressive: showing thoughts and feelings openly

Antonyms

reserved

reserved: keeping thoughts and feelings to oneself

tight-lipped

tight-lipped: deliberately refusing to speak up

How Strong Is It? — quiet → talkative → outspoken → vocal

quiet vs. vocal

quiet vs. vocal: Quiet marks the opposite end of the scale from vocal — keeping opinions unspoken rather than airing them.

talkative vs. vocal

talkative vs. vocal: Talkative people simply talk a lot about anything; vocal is stronger and more focused, openly and persistently voicing opinions.

outspoken vs. vocal

outspoken vs. vocal: Outspoken means frank and direct when a topic comes up, while vocal suggests actively and repeatedly speaking up without waiting to be asked.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — voc

Root — voc: voice; to call (Latin (vox, vocis, 'voice'))

Suffix — -al

Suffix — -al: relating to, characteristic of (Latin (-alis))

Put it together

Put it together: Voc- is Latin for 'voice,' and -al means 'relating to' — so vocal literally means 'relating to the voice.' A vocal person gives their opinions a voice, saying them out loud, openly and often.

Use the root in a new word: vocalize

Use the root in a new word: vocalize: The shy student slowly learned to vocalize her ideas during group projects.

Root Check

Word Choice

neutral

Vocal is the right word when someone openly and freely expresses opinions — whether at a meeting, online, or in conversation. For quiet, private disagreement, words like 'reserved' or 'quiet' fit better.
